summary: CCC-built 79-ft-6-in tower near Norwich, staffed 1936-1946; dismantled and moved near Brookfield in 1948; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 79-foot-6-inch International Derrick tower, provided to New York State by the US Forest Service
facts.status_note: Dismantled and moved to a site near Brookfield in 1948; no source describes the Chenango Lake site today.

events.note: CCC erected the tower; footings completed in 1934 and the tower in 1935

Staffed 1936 through 1943 and again in 1946, the last year listed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A July 1946 newspaper report, quoted by the Eastern lookouts site, said the tower would move to Brookfield once a foundation was ready. The Searchable list dates the dismantling and move to 1948. The story gives 1948 as the move year and treats 1946 as the plan.

sources.title: Searchable list of NY Fire Towers
sources.publisher: New York State Chapter, Forest Fire Lookout Association

notes_for_editor: Built, staffing and the 1948 move rest on the Searchable list; the Eastern lookouts site supplies the 1946 plan and the Brookfield newspaper quote. Nothing read describes the Chenango Lake site or the Brookfield site today. The Southern Tier and Adirondack list pages on nysfiretowers.com are in the cache, but their URLs could not be confirmed, so they are not cited. The Brookfield tower is treated as the moved structure and its removal in 1983 is taken from the Searchable list.
